partners.mechanism_chain: MTHFR (HGNC:7478) —DISRUPTS→ 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate (CHEBI:17983); 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate (CHEBI:17983) —LEADS_TO→ One-carbon metabolism (GO:0006079); One-carbon metabolism (GO:0006079) —INCREASES→ Homocysteine (CHEBI:17637); One-carbon metabolism (GO:0006079) —LEADS_TO→ Elevated homocysteine (HP:0002141); SLC19A1 (HGNC:10970) —DISRUPTS→ Tetrahydrofolate (CHEBI:17545); Tetrahydrofolate (CHEBI:17545) —LEADS_TO→ One-carbon metabolism (GO:0006079); One-carbon metabolism (GO:0006079) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). Loss-of-function mutations in MTHFR disrupt the conversion of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, leading to decreased remethylation of homocysteine to methionine, resulting in elevated homocysteine levels (Disease A). Concurrently, mutations in SLC19A1, which transports folate, impair the overall availability of tetrahydrofolate for one-carbon metabolism. This deficiency impacts purine and pyrimidine synthesis, crucial for lymphocyte proliferation and function, leading to immunodeficiency (Disease B). Both diseases converge on the central pathway of one-carbon metabolism, highlighting a shared mechanism despite distinct primary causal genes for each disease.
